comments.body:
═══ OPERATOR QUESTION ANSWERED: louder error, or deliberate graceful fallback? NEITHER — the gate's
failure handling is already correct. The gap is WHERE the error is raised and WHAT it says. ═══

**TRACED, so the fix does not change the wrong thing.** An unresolvable provider is NOT swallowed:
`coverage.llm_unavailable` → `review_bot/adapter.py:_coverage_gap_reason` returns `"llm-unavailable"`
→ the adapter calls `_block(gap, ...)` → decision **BLOCK** (a `-1` veto), with a message that
already separates infrastructure from code:

    rebar code review coverage gap — the review LLM was unavailable (<llm_error>). Fail-closed
    veto (infrastructure, not your code); re-run once the gate/scanner is healthy.

So a misconfiguration CANNOT pass silently, and the gate already fails closed. **That behaviour
should not change.** Two narrower things should:

**1. FAIL FAST AT CONFIG TIME, not at call time.** Dropping an explicitly configured `provider` is
not a runtime outage — it is a CONFIGURATION error, and it is currently reported neither at config
load nor at resolution. It surfaces ~20 LLM-seconds later, wearing an outage's clothes. A class whose
`provider` + `model` cannot be composed into a valid target should raise `LLMConfigError` where the
config is read, naming the class, the configured provider, the model id, and the reason.

**2. THE MESSAGE CURRENTLY CONTRADICTS THE OPERATOR'S OWN CONFIG.** What they see is:

    unknown provider 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1';
    registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']

They configured `provider = "bedrock"`, and the message says `bedrock` IS registered — so it reads as
"rebar's Bedrock support is broken" or "my credentials are wrong". The true cause (a colon in the
model id silently voided the provider setting) is unguessable from it. The string it blames is not a
provider the operator ever typed; it is most of their model id. Any fix must make the diagnosis name
the actual mistake.

**GRACEFUL FALLBACK IS THE WRONG CHOICE HERE — recommending explicitly against it.** Falling back to
`cfg.model` / a default provider would mean silently reviewing on a DIFFERENT provider than
configured. That is the exact failure this epic exists to remove: its origin was 41 of 42 calls
silently reaching direct Anthropic. Bedrock is normally chosen for data-residency, procurement or
contractual reasons, so a silent substitution is worse than a loud stop — it produces a cutover that
looks complete and is not. Fail closed (already) + fail fast (to add); never fall back.

**CLIENT-CONFUSION ASSESSMENT (the operator's first question): YES, and the likely path is short.**
The canonical id is what the AWS console and docs display, so `...-v1:0` is the string an operator
will paste. Nothing warns at config load. Reviews then start vetoing every change with an
"unavailable" message that contradicts their config. The cost is misdirected debugging against a
BLOCKED MERGE QUEUE — the expensive kind of confusion, on the critical path.

**ADDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA implied by the above** (folding in rather than leaving to be
re-derived):
- [ ] a class whose configured `provider` + `model` cannot be composed into a valid target fails at
      CONFIG-READ time with `LLMConfigError`, naming the class, the provider, the model id and the
      reason — not at first LLM call
- [ ] no diagnostic anywhere reports a fragment of a model id as though it were a configured provider
- [ ] the gate's existing FAIL-CLOSED behaviour on a genuine outage is unchanged and still tested
      (this ticket must not turn a `-1` veto into a pass)
- [ ] no silent fallback to `cfg.model` or a default provider is introduced as part of the fix

═══ IMPLEMENTED, RED→GREEN — and I deviated from one of my own acceptance criteria; reasoning below
so the verifier and a reader judge it rather than discover it. ═══

**THE FIX.** The qualified/unqualified decision moves out of two independent colon scans into ONE
helper, `config.split_provider_qualifier`:

    _PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$")

    def split_provider_qualifier(model): 
        prefix, sep, rest = model.partition(":")
        if sep and rest and _PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE.match(prefix): return prefix, rest
        return None, model

Both former deciders now call it:
* `model_classes._resolve_target` — was `if ":" in model: return model` (which discarded the
  configured provider);
* `config.infer_provider` — was `model.split(":", 1)[0]` (which returned a fragment of the model id).

They were two separate wrong implementations of the same question, which is why they failed in the
same way; there is now one implementation and a test asserting they agree.

**RED FIRST, CONFIRMED.** `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py`: pre-fix **6 failed, 15 passed**.
The 15 passing are the controls — already-qualified strings not double-prefixed, the unversioned
alias that always worked, and name-based inference — so the 6 failures could not be "nothing
resolves". Post-fix 21/21. One failure message is worth keeping as the record of the bug's shape:
`infer_provider returned 'anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1'`.

**DEVIATION FROM AN AC, STATED PLAINLY.** The criterion says the decision should be made "against the
REGISTERED PROVIDER SET rather than by the presence of a colon". I did the second half but not the
first: the test is the prefix's SHAPE (an identifier: lowercase, digits, `_`, `-`, and crucially NO
DOTS), not membership in a provider registry. Reasons, in order of weight:
 1. **The registry is not reachable here.** `_resolve_target` runs during CONFIG RESOLUTION.
    The live set is `ProviderSession._builders` — an INSTANCE attribute needing an `LLMConfig` — plus
    `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`, which imports `pydantic_ai`. That is the OPTIONAL `[agents]`
    extra, and `rebar.llm` is deliberately stdlib-only at import. Consulting it would make config
    parsing depend on an optional package.
 2. **A hand-maintained whitelist would defeat the AC's own stated purpose** — "so a future provider
    name needs no second edit here". A whitelist needs an edit per provider; the shape test needs
    none, and already accepts names this repo does not register (`openai-chat`, `openai-responses`,
    `google_genai`), which are covered by tests.
 3. **The discriminator is factually dots.** Provider names in this stack are identifiers; Bedrock
    model ids are dotted (`us.anthropic.…`, `anthropic.…`). That is what the versioned-vs-alias
    evidence showed, and it is checked against both shapes.
If the operator prefers the registry reading, the honest cost is either an optional-import dependency
in config parsing or a whitelist that needs maintaining — I judged the shape test strictly better and
am flagging it rather than quietly re-interpreting the criterion.

**NOT DONE, and it is NOT in this ticket's description ACs** — the config-time fail-fast I proposed in
the earlier design comment (raise `LLMConfigError` at config read for a class whose provider/model
cannot be composed). With the qualifier fixed, the reported failure can no longer arise from a colon,
so this is now about a DIFFERENT input (a genuine typo like `provider = "bedrok"`), which still
surfaces late as an "outage". Worth its own ticket rather than widening this one; the gate's
fail-closed behaviour is untouched either way.

**REGRESSION SURFACE.** `infer_provider` has wide fan-in, so it was the risk. 656 passed across the
provider/model-class/runner/workflow areas (`test_model_class_ladder`, `test_model_classes`,
`test_bedrock_provider`, `test_llm_provider_factory`, `test_openai_compatible_provider`,
`test_pydantic_ai_runner`, `test_code_review_verifier_class`, all of `tests/unit/workflow/`).
`make typecheck` clean (407 files), `make lint` clean. Full unit suite running.

**Still-unqualified colon splits left alone deliberately:** `runner.py:328` and `providers.py:215`
split an ALREADY-QUALIFIED `resolved` string, where splitting on the first colon is correct and the
fix does not change their inputs; `evals/eval.py:101-102` is eval-only. Naming them so a reader does
not have to re-derive that they were considered.

comments.body:
═══ GERRIT 1189: Verified +1, LLM-Review -1 — and the -1 is an INFRA veto, not a finding. Do not
"fix" the diff. ═══

    Verified    +1   (full CI: suite + lint + typecheck, green against this patch set)
    LLM-Review  -1   [LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)]
                     "the code review could not run. Fail-closed veto (infrastructure, not your
                      code); re-run once the gate/scanner is healthy."

CONTRIBUTING.md §2c is explicit on this exact tag: a coverage-gap `-1` means the review could not run,
is **not your code**, and "**a maintainer re-triggers it once infra recovers, don't 'fix' your diff**".
So the required action is a re-trigger by someone who can vote, NOT an amend. Recording that here so a
later reader does not mistake this for an unaddressed review finding, and does not churn the change.

**RULED OUT: that this change caused it.** `review-error` has exactly three sources
(`review_bot/adapter.py:196,211,214`): the gate import failed, `produce_code_review_verdict` raised,
or it returned a malformed verdict. This change edits `infer_provider`, which the gate uses, so it had
to be checked rather than assumed:
 * **`Verified +1` is the strongest single datum** — CI ran the full suite, lint and typecheck against
   THIS patch set and passed. Locally: 6439 passed / 19 skipped, plus 656 in the provider/runner/
   workflow areas.
 * **The only behavioural change is for colon-bearing NON-identifier prefixes**, where
   `infer_provider` previously returned a garbage fragment and now returns None. Every caller was
   audited for None-sensitivity and all are safe: `runner.py:590` passes it to
   `usage_log.record(provider=...)`, which omits an absent value; `model_classes.py:233` is
   `provider or infer_provider(...)` guarded by `if resolved_provider else model`;
   `anthropic_model.py:174` does `prov or ""` then `if prefix else m`; `sizing.py:348` is
   `if provider else bare` inside a best-effort try/except.
   `providers.py:172` LOOKS like a caller but is **pydantic-ai's own `infer_provider`** — a shadowed
   name, a different function. Noting it because a grep for callers finds it and it would be easy to
   mis-attribute.
 * **No working configuration regresses**: the strings whose result changed are exactly the ones that
   were already broken (an unqualified versioned Bedrock id), which is the bug this ticket fixes.

**MOST LIKELY CAUSE, stated as a suspicion not a conclusion:** this session has been running heavy
concurrent LLM load (two provider sweeps, several live gate runs, five parallel plan reviews, and four
parallel implementation subagents). If the review bot shares that quota, a throttle would make
`produce_code_review_verdict` raise, and the adapter fail-closes on ANY exception. That is the
designed behaviour working correctly — and it is worth noting that the fail-closed design is exactly
what I verified earlier when asked whether a provider misconfiguration could pass silently: it cannot.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ OSS COMPARISON REFUTES MY OWN JUSTIFICATION, and exposes a SECOND silent drop still present in
the first version of this fix. Reworked. ═══

Researched at the operator's request: how do popular, actively-maintained multi-provider projects
decide "is this string already provider-qualified?"

**1. REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP IS THE NORM. No project uses a shape/pattern rule.** LangChain
(`prefix in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`), LiteLLM (`prefix in litellm.provider_list`), pydantic-ai
(`infer_provider_class` raises on an unknown provider), Vercel AI SDK (`NoSuchProviderError` listing
`availableProviders`), simonw/llm (flat exact-match registry). So my deviation has no precedent.

**2. MY STATED REASON FOR DEVIATING IS ANSWERABLE, and three projects show how.** I argued the
registry was unreachable at config-resolution time without importing the optional `[agents]` extra.
But LangChain's `_BUILTIN_PROVIDERS` is a module-level dict of provider name → LAZY IMPORT
COORDINATES (`"bedrock": ("langchain_aws", "ChatBedrock", ...)`) — consulting the NAME SET imports
nothing. LiteLLM's `provider_list` is explicitly lazy-loaded with the comment "to avoid importing
LlmProviders at import time" — the same constraint I have, already solved. The design move is to
separate "which names are providers" (a static string set) from "what implements them" (downstream).
So the objection was mine, not the architecture's.

**3. THE BIGGEST FINDING — the real fix is GUARD ORDER, and I had not implemented it.** LangChain
uses `:` as its separator AND is immune to this bug, because of the FIRST condition in its test:

    if (not model_provider                                      # <-- explicit provider WINS
        and ":" in model
        and model.split(":", 1)[0] in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS): ...

An explicitly configured provider short-circuits the scan entirely, so no punctuation in a model id
can overrule it. **My first version still scanned first**, and I confirmed the resulting hole by
experiment:

    _resolve_target("openai:gpt-4o", provider="bedrock")  ->  'openai:gpt-4o'

The configured `provider = "bedrock"` is STILL SILENTLY DISCARDED. That is the SAME DEFECT CLASS this
ticket is about — dropping an explicit instruction — merely reached by a different input. Fixing the
colon test alone left half the bug standing.

**REWORKED.** `_resolve_target` now checks a configured provider FIRST: matching inline qualifier →
unchanged (no double-prefix); CONFLICTING qualifier → `LLMConfigError` naming both providers; no
qualifier → prefix it. Only when nothing is configured does it fall through to the qualifier scan and
then inference. Three new tests, including the control that agreement stays silent. 24/24 green; 652
passed across the provider/runner/workflow areas; lint and typecheck clean.

Chose to RAISE on a contradiction rather than pick a winner: either choice discards an explicit
instruction, which is exactly what this ticket exists to stop. It is also consistent with the
fail-fast direction already recorded on this ticket, and with prevailing practice — no researched
project silently drops a configured provider, and LiteLLM goes further, ASSERTING the configured
provider onto the string (`if custom_llm_provider and model.split("/")[0] != custom_llm_provider`).

**4. SEPARATOR: keep `:`.** pydantic-ai's own `KnownModelName` contains TWO-COLON entries
(`'bedrock:anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'`), so "provider, first colon, then a model name
that may itself contain colons" is exactly our runtime's grammar — we are compatible. `/` (LiteLLM,
OpenRouter) is collision-free for Bedrock and is arguably the better choice, but no project was found
regretting or migrating a separator, and changing ours would be a breaking config change for no
correctness gain now that the guard order is right.

**5. STILL OUTSTANDING, and now better motivated than when I first deferred it.** The shape test
remains in place for the no-configured-provider path, and it cannot produce the diagnostic a registry
can: a typo'd provider still passes silently —
`_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok") -> 'bedrok:claude-opus-4-8'` — where a registry would
raise "unknown provider 'bedrok'; valid: [...]". Switching that path to registry membership carries
real regression risk (an identifier-shaped provider valid in pydantic-ai but absent from our static
list would start being treated as unqualified and double-prefixed), so it wants its own ticket and
its own curated list rather than a same-change edit. Filing that separately.

A third option worth recording because our own runtime took it: pydantic-ai REMOVED bare-name
inference in v2.0.0b1 — `Agent('gpt-5')` now raises and you must write `openai:gpt-5`. If rebar
required explicit qualification the ambiguity would not exist at all. That is the cleanest end state
and the natural direction of travel, at the cost of a breaking config change.

compiled_state.description:
# `_resolve_target`'s "already provider-qualified" test is `":" in model`, and real Bedrock ids contain a colon

## Impact, stated first

**Any model class configured with `provider = "bedrock"` and a CANONICAL versioned Bedrock model id
is broken, and it fails with an error that names the wrong thing.** Canonical Bedrock ids carry a
version suffix containing a colon — `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`,
`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0` — which is the majority form of the ids AWS publishes.
Only the unversioned aliases (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`)
happen to work. This is in the middle of what epic 061c ships ("first-class AWS Bedrock provider").

## Mechanism, confirmed by experiment (no LLM spend)

`model_classes._resolve_target` decides whether to prefix the configured provider by asking whether
the model string already contains a colon:

    def _resolve_target(model: str, provider: str | None) -> str:
        # Already provider-qualified -- return as-is, never double-prefix.
        if ":" in model:
            return model
        resolved_provider = provider or infer_provider(model)
        return f"{resolved_provider}:{model}" if resolved_provider else model

A versioned Bedrock id satisfies `":" in model` for the WRONG reason — the colon is inside its
version suffix, not a provider separator — so the function returns the bare model and the
operator's explicit `provider = "bedrock"` is silently discarded:

    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",              "bedrock")
      -> "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"                      # correct
    _resolve_target("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", "bedrock")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"                 # provider LOST
    _resolve_target("anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0",     "bedrock")
      -> "anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0"                     # provider LOST

Downstream that unqualified string is read back as `provider:model` on the FIRST colon, so:

    infer_provider("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0")
      -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1"

…and the provider factory rejects it. Reproduced end-to-end through the real class table:

    parse_class_slots({"standard": {"model": "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0",
                                    "provider": "bedrock"}})
    resolve_class("standard", slots) -> "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"

## Observed live (this is how it was found)

A real `rebar review-code` run with `standard` pointed at the versioned Bedrock haiku id produced:

    verdict: INDETERMINATE, llm_ran: False
    llm_error: "step 'verify' failed: unknown provider
                'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1';
                registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']"

The whole gate degraded to INDETERMINATE. Note how misleading the message is: the operator
configured `provider = "bedrock"` — which IS registered — and the error blames a "provider" that is
actually most of their model id.

## Why the current test cannot simply be tightened to "split on the last colon"

The two forms are genuinely ambiguous on a naive scan: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains TWO
colons, and `us.anthropic.…-v1:0` contains one. Splitting on the first colon mis-reads the second
form; splitting on the last mis-reads the first. The distinguishing fact is not colon position but
whether the prefix names a REGISTERED PROVIDER — the same set the error message already prints.

## Acceptance criteria

**Delivered in TWO STAGES.** This ticket's change fixed the reported failure and the guard order; the
alignment with prevailing practice is delivered by child `7b22` and this ticket does not close until it
does. The split is recorded here rather than left implicit, because the original AC below asked for the
registry in one step and the implementation shipped a shape test instead — an OSS survey then found the
registry is the norm and that the reason for deviating was answerable. See the comments.

### This ticket's change (done)

- [x] a configured `provider` is honoured for a model id containing a colon: a class configured
      `{model: "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0", provider: "bedrock"}` resolves to
      `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
- [x] an ALREADY-qualified string is still not double-prefixed: `bedrock:us.anthropic.…-v1:0` stays
      unchanged (this is the property the original test was protecting and it must not regress)
- [x] the qualified/unqualified decision is NO LONGER made by the presence of a colon, and both
      deciders (`_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`) route through ONE shared function
      (`split_provider_qualifier`) so they cannot drift apart — the original defect was two
      independent implementations of one question
- [x] **GUARD ORDER: an explicitly configured `provider` is checked FIRST, before the model string is
      scanned at all**, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule or discard it. Added after the
      OSS survey showed this is the actual fix for the bug CLASS: LangChain uses `:` as its separator
      and is immune purely because `not model_provider` is the first condition it tests. Without this,
      `_resolve_target("openai:gpt-4o", provider="bedrock")` still silently dropped the configured
      provider — the same defect reached by a different input
- [x] a conflicting configured-provider / inline-qualifier pair RAISES rather than silently picking a
      winner, since either choice discards an explicit instruction
- [x] a bare id with no configured provider still infers as it does today (back-compat: every
      existing unversioned value resolves byte-for-byte unchanged)
- [x] tests cover BOTH Bedrock id shapes — unversioned alias and canonical `...-v1:0` — because
      the unversioned form passes even against the bug and is what hid it
- [x] `infer_provider` agrees with the qualifier on every shape the tests cover
- [x] the reported failure mode is gone: no diagnostic reports a fragment of a model id as though it
      were a configured provider

### Delegated to child `7b22` (this ticket stays open until it closes)

- [ ] the qualified/unqualified decision is made against the REGISTERED PROVIDER SET rather than by
      prefix shape, so a future provider name needs no second edit here — the mechanism every
      comparable project uses (LangChain, LiteLLM, pydantic-ai, Vercel AI SDK, simonw/llm)
- [ ] a provider name that is not registered produces a diagnostic naming the invalid provider and
      listing the valid ones. This is the capability a shape test CANNOT provide, and it is why the
      rework is required rather than optional: a typo'd provider
      (`_resolve_target("claude-opus-4-8", "bedrok")`) currently passes silently
- [ ] back-compat is enumerated and tested against the runtime registries, since a stricter test
      risks breaking provider names that work today but are absent from a static list

## Notes

Found while gathering ticket 3768's non-default-provider evidence, which the bug BLOCKS for any
versioned id; that evidence was obtained with unversioned aliases as a workaround. Not folded into
b690 (whose change is already `LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1`) because it is an unrelated seam with
its own back-compat surface. Filed under epic 061c per the operator's standing ruling that provider-
seam wiring is epic work; the epic's mandate is to ship without bugs, so flagging rather than
deferring silently.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock: a configured provider is silently DROPPED for any model id containing a colon (the canonical '...-v1:0' form)
